correctness.rationale: The original multiplication gives S−x_i²=x_i for each coordinate and therefore x_i²+x_i=S. Every solution has at most two values. With k occurrences of u and n−k of v, Vieta gives v=−1−u, and the precise quadratic (n−1)u²+(2(n−k)−1)u+(n−k)=0. Its discriminant and the exceptional coincidence u=−1/2 give the first r_k; its linear degeneration when p divides n−1 gives the second. Every nonconstant solution is counted twice by complementing its value classes, producing the exact formula. All roots lie in F_{p²}, implying the two-cycle Frobenius zeta formula. Independently, direct exhaustive enumeration for F3,F5,F7,F11 and F9 matches the formulas; finite checks supplement but do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: Individual idempotents are fixed points of the defining quadratic evolution dynamics, a natural invariant independent of the algebra-regularity notion E²=E and of the known automorphism group. The theorem completely enumerates them for the canonical complete-graph algebra in every odd finite field and every dimension, including previously excluded singular adjacency characteristics. The uniform splitting over F_{p²}, square-class-sensitive counts, and closed zeta factorization provide structural arithmetic information about the whole family, not an arbitrarily selected small instance.
